posts.title: 2026 tourist taxes by city: what you actually pay per night
posts.summary: A city-by-city table of 2026 tourist taxes, visitor levies and overnight fees, compiled from the same official-source research as our destination pages. No invented rates.
posts.body:
Hotel rates are not the bill. In 2026 a growing list of cities add a tourist tax, visitor levy, green tax or climate fee on top of the room, and several of those rates moved this year. The numbers below are the ones we already published, destination by destination, after checking operator and government sources at the time of writing. Where a figure is a percentage of the room rate, do the maths on the net rate, not the package price you saw on a booking site.

This is not a complete world list. It is every destination on RuinMyTrip where we could pin down a current overnight tax. Day-tripper access fees (Venice) and airport departure fees (Maldives) are called out separately because they are not the same thing as a hotel tax, even though they hit the same trip budget.

Overnight tourist taxes in 2026

City2026 rateHow it is charged
Amsterdam12.5% of net room price, the highest in Europe, plus 21% Dutch VAT on accommodation from 1 January 2026Per night, on the room. The coalition plans a rise from 12.5% to 16% in 2027. Stacked, tax is roughly a third of the quoted room rate.
Barcelona4.50 EUR Catalan regional rate plus 5 EUR city surcharge per person per night, plus 10% VAT, from 1 April 2026About 12 EUR per person per night at five-star hotels (up from 7.50 EUR in 2025), 8.40 EUR at four-star, 9.50 EUR on short-term rentals. The city surcharge rises 1 EUR a year through 2029.
Berlin7.5% of the net accommodation price (Ubernachtungsteuer), unchanged since 1 January 2025Applies to business stays as well as leisure, since 1 April 2024. Operators file quarterly via ELSTER.
Edinburgh5% visitor levy on paid overnight accommodation, first 5 consecutive nightsTook effect 24 July 2026. Applies to bookings made on or after 1 October 2025. Projected to raise up to 50 million pounds a year.
Hong Kong3% hotel accommodation taxReintroduced in 2025, still in effect in 2026.
KyotoFive-tier lodging tax from March 2026: 200 yen (under 6,000), 400 yen (6,000-19,999), 1,000 yen (20,000-49,999), 4,000 yen (50,000-99,999), 10,000 yen (100,000+)Per person per night, based on the room rate band.
Lisbon4 EUR per person per nightGuests aged 13 and over, capped at 7 nights. Raised from 2 EUR on 1 September 2024.
MaldivesResort green tax 12 USD per person per night (doubled from 6 USD on 1 January 2025). Smaller properties collect 6 USD.Earmarked for reef protection. On top of that, airport departure fees for foreigners rose to 50 USD economy, 120 USD business, 240 USD first class.
Milan10 EUR per person per night at 4-star hotels; 9.50 EUR for vacation rentals and tourist apartmentsEffective 1 April 2026, Municipal Council resolution no. 144 of 12 February 2026.
NiceRoughly 1.50 to 6.00 EUR per person per nightUnclassified properties (most short-term rentals) are charged 1 to 5% of the per-person nightly rate excluding VAT, capped at the highest local rate.
Osaka200 yen (5,000 to under 15,000 yen rooms), 400 yen (15,000 to under 20,000), 500 yen (20,000+). Rooms under 5,000 yen are exempt.Per person per night since 1 September 2025. From 1 March 2026 it is charged separately from the room rate and paid on-site even for prepaid bookings.
Porto3 EUR per person per night, up from about 2 EURCapped at 7 nights, 21 EUR maximum per trip.
PragueCZK 50 per person per nightPrague 1 has proposed about CZK 175 (roughly 7 EUR). That is a proposal, not the current rate.
Reykjavik800 ISK per lodging unit per night for hotels and guesthouses; 400 ISK for campsites and motorhome pitchesIceland lodging tax effective 1 January 2025. Charged per unit, not per person.
Rome4 EUR (1-star) to 10 EUR (5-star) per person per night; flat 6 EUR for short-term rentalsCapped at 10 nights.
SantoriniClimate resilience tax 2 EUR (1-2 star) to 15 EUR (5-star) per nightHigh season only, April through October.
VancouverCombined 5.5% municipal accommodation tax (3% MRDT + 2.5% Major Events MRDT)The extra 2.5% runs through 31 January 2030 to help fund World Cup costs.
ViennaOrtstaxe 5% of the room rate from 1 July 2026 (up from 3.2%)A further rise to 8% is scheduled for 1 July 2027.

Not a hotel tax, still on the bill

Venice charges a day-tripper access fee on 60 days between April and July 2026: 5 EUR if you book more than three days ahead, 10 EUR inside that window, 08:30 to 16:00. Overnight guests and residents are exempt. That is a gate fee, not an overnight tax. The full calendar is in our Venice access fee 2026 note.

London is developing an overnight visitor levy under the English Devolution and Community Empowerment Bill, floated at either 2 to 4 pounds per person per night or about 5% of the room. It is not in force. Do not budget it as a current tax.

How to actually budget it

Percentage taxes (Amsterdam, Berlin, Edinburgh, Hong Kong, Vancouver, Vienna, Kyoto's bands) scale with the room. A 200 EUR net night in Amsterdam is about 25 EUR in tourist tax before the 21% VAT. Flat per-person taxes (Lisbon, Porto, Barcelona's surcharge, Milan, Rome) scale with the number of people and the number of nights, then usually cap. A family of four in Lisbon for a week hits the 7-night cap at 112 EUR. That is not a rounding error.

Booking sites sometimes collect the tax and sometimes do not. Assume it is extra until the confirmation says otherwise. For the destination-level version of these numbers, including the tickets and scams that sit next to the tax, start at the city page rather than this table.

posts.title: Venice access fee 2026: 60 days, 5 or 10 euros, overnight guests exempt
posts.summary: The 2026 contributo di accesso runs 60 days between April and July. Book more than three days out and it is 5 euros. Inside that window it is 10. Overnight guests do not pay it.
posts.body:
Venice is not charging you to look at the water. It is charging day-trippers to walk into the historic centre on the days the city has decided it cannot absorb another surge. In 2026 that calendar is the largest the scheme has used.

When the fee applies in 2026

The contributo di accesso applies on 60 days between April and July: every Friday, Saturday and Sunday from 3 April through 26 July, plus 6 April, the week beginning 27 April, and the week beginning 1 June. It is enforced from 08:30 to 16:00. Arrive as a day-tripper on one of those days, in that window, and you owe it.

What it costs

5 euros if you book more than three days ahead. 10 euros if you buy inside the three-day window. In 2025, 49% of the people who paid paid the higher rate. That is not a trivia statistic, it is the default outcome for anyone who treats the fee as a walk-up ticket.

Residents and overnight guests are exempt. Overnight guests still register. If you are already paying for a hotel night in the city, the fee is not stacked on top. Two separate day trips, on two fee days, with two last-minute 10 euro payments, is the expensive version of Venice. One overnight stay is usually cheaper in total.

Has it reduced the crowds?

Not in any way a visitor will notice. In 2025 the scheme collected 5,421,425 euros from 723,497 payments, nearly double 2024's 2.4 million euros from 485,062 payments across a 29-day run. The historic centre is down to 47,995 residents. Peak day-tripper counts have been put as high as 85,000. The fee raised money. It did not restore a quiet city.

Around San Marco the other costs are worse than the fee: restaurant overcharging is systematic, a single vaporetto ride is 9.50 euros, and gondola prices above the posted association rate are a documented pattern. The 5 euro access fee is the line item that is trivial to get right and embarrassing to get wrong.

Book it when you book the train. The destination page and the Venice 2026 guide cover the rest of the bill.

posts.title: Park Guell ticket price 2026: 18 euros after an 80 percent jump
posts.summary: Park Guell adult admission is 18 euros in 2026, up from 10 euros, capped at 1,400 visitors an hour. Sagrada Familia is 26 euros, or 36 with towers, plus a centenary surcharge from June through December.
posts.body:
Barcelona's two most famous Gaudi sites both got more expensive in 2026, and neither is a walk-up anymore.

Park Guell

Adult admission is 18 euros, an 80% jump from 10 euros at the start of 2026. Entry is capped at 1,400 visitors per hour on a timed ticket. Book online days ahead. Showing up at the gate in July is how you spend an afternoon in Barcelona not seeing Park Guell.

Sagrada Familia

A standard ticket with audio guide is 26 euros in 2026. Tower access is 36 euros. A centenary surcharge of 2 to 5 euros applies from June through December 2026. Timed entry is mandatory. This is also not a walk-up.

The rest of the 2026 Barcelona bill

The tourist tax effectively doubled on 1 April 2026: 4.50 EUR Catalan regional rate plus 5 EUR city surcharge per person per night, plus 10% VAT. Five-star stays land around 12 EUR per person per night in tax alone. Short-term rentals are about 9.50 EUR. The city surcharge keeps climbing 1 EUR a year through 2029, and every remaining tourist-apartment licence is set to expire by November 2028.

Transit is still the cheap line: a T-Casual 10-ride card is 13 euros in one zone. That does not offset an 8 euro Park Guell increase plus a doubled hotel tax plus a Sagrada surcharge, but it is the one 2026 number in Barcelona that barely moved.

Full context, including pickpocketing hotspots on Metro Lines 1 and 3 and the Airbnb countdown, is on the Barcelona destination page and the 2026 Barcelona guide.

posts.title: Amsterdam tourist tax 2026: 12.5 percent plus 21 percent VAT
posts.summary: Amsterdam charges Europe's highest tourist tax at 12.5 percent of the net room rate, stacked on a 21 percent VAT that took effect 1 January 2026. The coalition plans 16 percent in 2027.
posts.body:
Amsterdam is no longer a cheap city that happens to have a canal tax. In 2026 the overnight bill is a 12.5 percent tourist tax, already the highest in Europe, stacked on Dutch VAT on hotel accommodation that jumped from 9 percent to 21 percent on 1 January 2026. On a 200 euro net room, the tourist tax is about 25 euros before VAT. Together they take roughly a third of the quoted rate.

What you pay in 2026

The tourist tax is 12.5 percent of the net room price, per night. It is a percentage, so it scales with the hotel. The VAT change is national, not an Amsterdam extra, but it lands on the same line. The new municipal coalition has said it plans to raise the tourist tax from 12.5 percent to 16 percent in 2027, and later toward 20 percent. That is a plan, not the current rate. Budget 12.5 percent plus 21 percent VAT now.

Why the city is doing this

Amsterdam logged 23.7 million overnight stays in 2025, about 800,000 more than 2024, while running the Stay Away campaign against stag-party search traffic. A citywide hotel bed freeze has been in effect since November 2024. From 1 April 2026, short-term holiday rentals in the city centre and De Pijp are capped at 15 nights a year. Ocean cruise dockings are capped at 100 per year from 2026. None of that reduced demand enough to drop the tax.

What else hits the same trip

Anne Frank House tickets are 16.50 euros for adults in 2026, 7 euros for ages 10-17, and they release every Tuesday at 10:00 Amsterdam time, six weeks ahead. Popular midday slots have been reported gone in two to three minutes. A GVB 24-hour transit ticket is 10 euros; OVpay GVB Max caps the day at 10.50 euros. Bike rental from a reputable shop is 12 to 18 euros a day, and the city estimates around 28,500 actual bike thefts a year.

The destination page and the Amsterdam 2026 guide cover Red Light District rules (100 euro outdoor cannabis fine, no photos of windows). Compare the tax against other cities in the 2026 tourist tax table.

posts.title: Kyoto lodging tax 2026: five tiers, up to 10,000 yen per person per night
posts.summary: From 1 March 2026 Kyoto charges a five-tier lodging tax per person per night, from 200 yen under 6,000 yen rooms to 10,000 yen at 100,000 yen and above. The top band is the steepest in Japan.
posts.body:
Kyoto restructured its lodging tax on 1 March 2026. It is charged per person, per night, not per room, and the top band is the steepest lodging tax in Japan. A couple in a 120,000 yen room is 20,000 yen of tax for that night, on top of the room.

The five tiers, from 1 March 2026

Room rate bandTax per person per night
Under 6,000 yen200 yen
6,000 to 19,999 yen400 yen
20,000 to 49,999 yen1,000 yen
50,000 to 99,999 yen4,000 yen
100,000 yen and above10,000 yen

Golden Week 2026 already showed what the top of the market looks like: Kyoto had the highest average hotel rate among six major Japanese cities at 48,900 yen. That is the 1,000 yen band for most rooms, 4,000 yen once you cross 50,000.

The rest of the 2026 squeeze

Kyoto drew 10.88 million foreign visitors in 2024. The 700 yen bus-only day pass is gone. The city-bus central-zone flat fare is 230 yen; the sightseeing limited express buses (EX100/EX101) are 500 yen adult. A Subway and Bus 1-Day Pass is 1,100 yen. Resident-priority bus pricing (about 200 yen for residents versus 350-400 yen for visitors) is announced for fiscal 2027, not in force yet.

The sites themselves are still cheap: Kinkaku-ji and Kiyomizu-dera are 500 yen for adults, Fushimi Inari is free and always open. Gion is the opposite of cheap if you ignore the signs: private alleys off Hanamikoji Street carry a 10,000 yen trespass fine.

Full planning notes are on the Kyoto destination page and the Kyoto 2026 trip planner. City-by-city comparison: 2026 tourist taxes.

posts.title: Edinburgh visitor levy 2026: 5 percent, first five nights, first in the UK
posts.summary: Edinburgh became the first UK city to charge a visitor levy on 24 July 2026: 5 percent on paid overnight accommodation for the first five consecutive nights. It applies to bookings made on or after 1 October 2025.
posts.body:
Edinburgh is the first UK city to put a visitor levy on the hotel bill. From 24 July 2026 it is 5 percent of paid overnight accommodation, charged on the first five consecutive nights of a stay, and projected to raise up to 50 million pounds a year. Bookings made before 1 October 2025 are exempt even if the trip itself is later. Bookings made on or after that date are not.

How the 5 percent actually works

It is a percentage of the room, not a flat per-person fee. A 200 pound night is 10 pounds of levy. Five nights is the cap: night six and after in the same stay do not add more levy. A one-night stay pays 5 percent once. A Fringe-week booking at 300 pounds a night for five nights is 75 pounds of levy on top of an already doubled or tripled room rate.

August is the real multiplier

The Edinburgh Festival Fringe runs 7 to 31 August 2026. Festival-month hostels run about 45 to 80 pounds for a dorm against 20 to 35 pounds in a normal month. Budget hotels 150 to 300 pounds against 55 to 140. Mid-range 250 to 500 against 140 to 280. The levy sits on top of that, it does not replace it. January to March and November are the 20 to 40 percent cheaper window.

Other 2026 line items

UK ETA for non-British/Irish visitors without UK immigration status is required from 25 February 2026. The fee rose from 16 to 20 pounds on 8 April 2026, valid up to two years, no child discount. Lothian Buses adult singles rose to 2.20 pounds on 22 February 2026. Edinburgh Trams airport-to-city is 7.90 pounds one way, frozen for 2026. Edinburgh Castle is about 21.50 to 23.50 pounds online, cheaper than the gate, on 30-minute timed slots.

The Royal Mile is one of the most complained-about tourist traps in the UK. Police Scotland logged 47 tourist-related thefts in 2025, down from 62 in 2024. Violent crime against visitors is rare. The levy is the new line item; the Fringe calendar is still the one that can actually ruin the budget.

More on the Edinburgh destination page and the 2026 Edinburgh guide. Compare other cities in the 2026 tourist tax table.
